newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco late-month unleaded continues slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco late-month unleaded continues slide.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent late-November spot unleaded gasoline basis continued to slide lower on Tuesday, reflecting weakness in the Midwest and Gulf Coast spot markets, traders said.
A two-cent a gallon drop in Group Three unleaded differentials weakened first-cycle December basis in the neighboring Chicago market, which wrapped up trade in November barrels, traders said.
"The Gulf Coast got slammed, and that (weakness) spread right up here," one trader said.

Midwest refineries were operating at 96.5 percent of rated capacity last week, continuing a frenetic pace begun after Clark Refining and Marketing restarted a fluid catalytic cracker at its 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery.
Despite the stepped up production, gasoline supplies were drawn down a net 377,000 barrels in the PADD II Midwest region, the American Petroleum Institute said late in the day.

High sulphur diesel barrels posted a 334,000 barrel build on the week, while low sulphur stocks in primary storage at regional refineries was pegged up 185,000 barrels, the trade group said in its weekly refined products inventory survey.
Group Three unleaded gasoline for late-month deliveries weakened to bids 0.75 cent a gallon under the print.
Chicago unleaded for first-cycle December deliveries was talked 2.0/2.75 cents a gallon over NYMEX January unleaded, with later deliveries 0.75/0.50 cent under the print.
Distillate differentials were largely unchanged late in the day from morning discussion, traders said.
